name: Brazil
note: A physician completes the federal Declaração de Óbito (by the IML for external-cause deaths), one copy goes to the health secretariat's mortality system, and a relative or other listed declarant takes another to the Registro Civil de Pessoas Naturais to register the death, in principle within 24 hours; no burial without the registry's certidão. Each registered death must then go to the INSS through SIRC within one business day, and the registry must also notify the Receita Federal and the State identity-card issuer, with no time set. The Receita marks the CPF "Titular Falecido" and anyone can check that status. The registration duties themselves (arts. 78–79 of Lei 6.015) still rest on the unreadable consolidated text and remain unverified.

steps.title: Physician completes the Declaração de Óbito
steps.who: The physician who attended the patient, or a substitute; for confirmed or suspected external-cause deaths, the physician of the medico-legal service (IML); in a place with no physician, the Cartório do Registro Civil, at the request of the person responsible for the deceased with two witnesses.
steps.summary: By statute the Declaração de Óbito is the SUS's official document attesting a death, and one copy must go to the civil registry and another to the health secretariat. Under Portaria SVS 116/2009, which the Ministry of Health's 2022 manual names as the rule in force, the attending physician issues it and the family takes a copy to the Cartório to obtain the certidão; art. 77 of the registry law makes the entry on the physician's attestation or, failing one, on that of two qualified witnesses.

steps.title: External-cause deaths certified by the medico-legal service (IML)
steps.who: The physicians of the medico-legal service (Instituto Médico-Legal); where there is no IML, any local physician or a professional appointed ad hoc by the judicial or police authority.
steps.trigger: A confirmed or suspected death from external causes (accident or violence).
steps.summary: For confirmed or suspected external-cause deaths the attending physician does not issue the Declaração de Óbito: it must be issued by the IML's physicians, whatever the time between the violent event and the death, or where there is no IML by a local physician or an ad hoc expert appointed by the judicial or police authority. The Code of Criminal Procedure's own rules on forensic examination were not read.

steps.title: Declare the death at the Registro Civil de Pessoas Naturais
steps.who: The persons listed in art. 79 in order (head of household, spouse, children, relatives, hospital administrators, attending physician, neighbours, police for found bodies).
steps.trigger: The death, with the Declaração de Óbito.

deadline.text: 24 hours, extendable to 15 days (longer for places far from the registry)

steps.summary: The death is registered at the civil registry of the place of death (or residence) in principle within 24 hours; where that is impossible, within the art. 50 periods (15 days, longer for distant places).

steps.title: Hospital administrators as declarants
steps.who: Administrators of hospitals and similar establishments.
steps.summary: Hospital administrators are among the persons bound to declare the death.

steps.title: No burial without the registry's death certidão
steps.who: The registry officer (oficial de registro civil) of the place of death or of the deceased's residence.
steps.summary: No burial without a certidão from the registry officer of the place of death, or of the deceased's residence where the death occurred away from home, issued after the death entry is drawn up.

steps.title: Certidão de óbito for any applicant
steps.who: Any person, without stating a reason.
steps.summary: Registry certificates may be requested by anyone without stating the reason or interest.

steps.title: Registry sends the death to the INSS through SIRC within one business day
steps.who: The titular of the Registro Civil de Pessoas Naturais.

deadline.text: em até 1 (um) dia útil; 5 dias úteis where the municipality has no internet access

steps.summary: The registry must send the INSS, through SIRC (which the INSS operates), the list of registered deaths within one business day, or five business days where the municipality has no internet access. Non-compliance or inexact information exposes the registry holder to the art. 92 penalty and to recovery action by the INSS.

steps.title: Federal and other public bodies obtain SIRC data on request
steps.who: SIRC, operated by the INSS under the CGSirc steering committee; public bodies that request the data (CGSirc member bodies need no authorisation).
steps.summary: SIRC captures and holds the registries' birth, marriage, death and stillbirth data. Public bodies at any level may be given it on a reasoned request authorised by CGSirc (member bodies without authorisation) and may load it into their own databases. Decreto 9.929 also asks registries to insert data preferably daily, by the 10th of the following month at the latest, which the one-business-day rule in Lei 8.212 art. 68 overrides for the INSS.

steps.title: Registry reports deaths to the Justiça Eleitoral
steps.who: Civil registry officers, to the electoral judge.
steps.trigger: Deaths of citizens of voting age registered in the month.

deadline.text: by the 15th of the following month

steps.summary: Officers must report each month the deaths of persons eligible to vote, for cancellation of their registration.

steps.title: Quarterly returns to IBGE
steps.summary: Registries send IBGE quarterly returns of births, marriages and deaths for vital statistics.

steps.title: Anyone may inform the Receita Federal of the death; the CPF becomes "Titular Falecido"
steps.who: Any person, solely to report the death, with the death certificate (or a birth or marriage certificate annotated with the death) and their own photo ID; heirs, the inventariante, spouse or relatives for other CPF acts.
steps.trigger: A person reports the death to the Receita Federal.
steps.summary: Once the Receita Federal has information of the death, the CPF status must be "Titular Falecido" and cannot return to "Regular". Anyone may report a death to the RFB, at a counter or remotely, on presenting the certificate.

steps.title: CPF updates from third-party data under convênios
steps.who: Receita Federal, on data supplied by parties to an information-exchange convênio; ARPEN-BR, the national association of civil registrars, is among the entities the RFB may contract with.
steps.trigger: Data made available under a convênio.
steps.summary: The RFB alters CPF records on information supplied by third parties under information-exchange convênios, and may conclude convênios with ARPEN-BR. Separately, art. 80 sole paragraph of the registry law obliges the registry itself to notify the Receita Federal of each death (step br-rfb-registry); no text read says how that notice is delivered or whether it runs through SIRC or a convênio.

steps.title: Registry notifies the Receita Federal of the death
steps.who: The civil registry officer who registered the death.
steps.latencyNote: comunicará o óbito à Receita Federal; no time set (Lei 6.015, art. 80, par. único)
steps.summary: Since Lei 13.114/2015 the registry law obliges the civil registry officer to notify the Receita Federal of each registered death, unless the deceased's age makes it manifestly unnecessary. The law sets no time limit or channel; how the notice reaches the CPF base is not stated in the texts read.

steps.title: Registry notifies the State public-security secretariat that issued the identity card
steps.who: The civil registry officer, to the Secretaria de Segurança Pública of the State that issued the deceased's cédula de identidade.
steps.latencyNote: comunicará o óbito ... à Secretaria de Segurança Pública; no time set (Lei 6.015, art. 80, par. único)
steps.summary: The same provision obliges the registry to notify the death to the public-security secretariat of the State that issued the deceased's identity card, the body that keeps the civil identification record, except where the deceased's age makes it manifestly unnecessary. No deadline is set.

steps.title: Declaração de Óbito copy goes to the health secretariat for the mortality system (SIM)
steps.who: The health establishment (or the IML, SVO or attending physician) sends the first copy of the DO to the municipal health secretariat; municipal and State secretariats pass the data up to the Ministry of Health.
steps.trigger: Issue of the Declaração de Óbito.

deadline.text: municipalities to the State within 30 days, and States to the national module within 60 days, after the end of the month of the death

steps.latencyNote: até 60 (sessenta) dias após o encerramento do mês de ocorrência (Portaria SVS 116/2009, art. 34)
steps.summary: Independently of registration, the statute requires one copy of the Declaração de Óbito to go to the State or municipal health secretariat. Under Portaria SVS 116/2009 the first copy goes to the municipal health secretariat, which must pass the data to the State within 30 days of the month's end; the State must transfer it to the national module within 60 days.

steps.title: Electronic certidões from any registry through SERP
steps.who: Civil registries, which must all join the Sistema Eletrônico dos Registros Públicos (SERP); under CNJ rules, through the Central de Informações de Registro Civil (CRC).
steps.summary: Every registry must join SERP, and anyone may ask any registry for an electronic certidão of an entry held at another registry through SERP, on terms set by the CNJ's Corregedoria Nacional. The CNJ provisions that run this through the CRC were not read.

steps.title: Public query of a CPF's status shows "Titular Falecido"
steps.who: Anyone, including banks and insurers, through the Receita Federal's Comprovante de Situação Cadastral no CPF (website or app).
steps.summary: The CPF's registration status, including "Titular Falecido", can be consulted publicly. It reflects only what the RFB has been told. SIRC itself is closed to private bodies except for anonymised research.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: In principle within 24 hours; where impossible, within the art. 50 periods (15 days, longer for distant places).

informantDuty.note: An ordered list in art. 79 runs from the head of household and relatives to hospital administrators, physicians, neighbours and police.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of the Declaração de Óbito; external-cause deaths are certified by the medico-legal service (IML) instead of the attending physician.

electronicRegistration.note: All registries must join the national electronic registry system (SERP), whose objectives include remote service over the internet and electronic certidões from any registry, and they transmit deaths to SIRC; whether a death can be declared remotely depends on CNJ rules that were not read.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No single population register in the legal sense: SIRC holds civil-registration data for public bodies, and the CPF base is kept by the Receita Federal.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration alone sends the death to the INSS through SIRC within one business day (Lei 8.212 art. 68), the registry must also notify the Receita Federal and the identity-card issuer (Lei 6.015 art. 80 sole paragraph, no time set), and other public bodies can obtain SIRC data on request. The monthly report to the electoral justice is unverified.

certificateAccess.note: Anyone may request a certidão without stating a reason.

privateSectorVerification.note: Anyone can consult a CPF's status publicly, which shows "Titular Falecido" once the Receita Federal has been told of the death; SIRC itself is open to private bodies only for anonymised research. SERP's objectives also include exchanging documents and information with users, financial institutions among them (Lei 14.382 art. 3 VII b), on CNJ terms not read.

gaps: www.planalto.gov.br answers every request with an origin block page ("Acesso Negado"), and www4.planalto.gov.br/legislacao and legislacao.planalto.gov.br answer with an F5 bot challenge; legislacao.presidencia.gov.br reports "SEI indisponível". All were left alone. camara.leg.br / www2.camara.gov.br, senado.leg.br, normas.leg.br, dadosabertos.camara.leg.br, www.tse.jus.br, www.cnj.jus.br, atos.cnj.jus.br, every state court host tried (tjsc, tjsp, tjmg, tjrj and others) and portal.cfm.org.br are egress-denied; www.ibge.gov.br answers 403 from the site; www.sirc.gov.br and sirc.dataprev.gov.br reset the connection; the LexML search page is behind a Senado "Verificação de segurança" challenge (its /urn/ records read, but carry metadata, not text). No consolidated text of any Brazilian law could be read. The MRE consular pages on www.gov.br that restate art. 79's list of declarants returned an image CAPTCHA on 28 October 2026 and were left alone.

Readable and used (28 October 2026): the Diário Oficial da União on www.in.gov.br (HTML of each act as enacted, back to about 2017) and, for older editions, the Imprensa Nacional's page-image archive on pesquisa.in.gov.br, which serves each DOU page as a PDF from 1990 onward (index.jsp?jornal=1&pagina=N&data=DD/MM/YYYY; the PDF itself comes from servlet/INPDFViewer with captchafield=firstAccess, which is the viewer's own first-access link, not a solved challenge). Editions before 1990 are not there, so the 1973 original and the 1975 republication of Lei 6.015 cannot be read. Also used: Receita Federal pages on www.gov.br and the Ministry of Health library (bvsms.saude.gov.br).

Unverified, consolidated text unreadable and no post-1990 amending act found that restates them: Lei 6.015/1973 arts. 17 (certidão to anyone), 49 (IBGE returns), 50 (15-day extension), 78 (24 hours), 79 (declarants) and 80 caput (content of the entry); CPP art. 162; Código Eleitoral art. 71 § 3º. Amending acts read in the DOU (Leis 13.114/2015, 13.484/2017, 14.382/2022) touch arts. 17 (§§ 1–2 only), 19, 77 and 80 (sole paragraph) but not the caput provisions relied on.

Lei 8.212 art. 68 and Lei 6.015 art. 77 were read only in the amending acts (Leis 13.846/2019 and 13.484/2017) as published in the DOU; a later amendment would not show. The art. 92 penalty itself was not read.

Decreto 9.929/2019 art. 8 § 1 (preferably daily, by the 10th of the following month) is looser than Lei 8.212 art. 68 (one business day, to the INSS); Resolução CGSirc 9/2024 defers to the art. 68 period. Recorded as the statute governing.
CRC Nacional: the CNJ provisions (Provimento 46/2015, now in the Código Nacional de Normas, Provimento CNJ 149/2023) were not read; cnj.jus.br is egress-denied.
Electoral: Código Eleitoral art. 71 § 3º and the TSE's rules on cancelling registrations were not read (planalto and tse.jus.br unreachable).

Lei 11.976/2009 and Portaria SVS/MS 116/2009 were read as published in the DOU (8 July 2009 and 12 February 2009). The Ministry of Health's 2022 DO manual still cites Portaria 116/2009 as the rule in force; whether it has since been folded into a consolidation ordinance was not checked.

Lei 6.015 art. 80 sole paragraph (registry notifies the Receita Federal and the identity-card issuer) was read only in Lei 13.114/2015 as published; Lei 14.382/2022 does not amend art. 80, but a later amendment would not show.

Receita Federal: IN RFB 2.172/2024 (as amended by IN RFB 2.236/2024) sets the "Titular Falecido" status, lets anyone report a death, and art. 9 III allows updates from convênio data. Lei 6.015 art. 80 sole paragraph obliges the registry to notify the RFB, but no text read says through which channel (SIRC, a convênio or otherwise) or how fast. The CPF public-query terms (which identifiers are needed) were not read.
